Hey! I totally get the struggle. That tablet is a great investment, but running heavy apps on older hardware can be a pain. Since you’re on a tight budget, let’s focus on some zero-cost tweaks that can actually make a difference.

First, let’s tackle the browser tab issue. Chrome and Edge are notorious memory hogs. You should enable the "Memory Saver" or "Efficiency Mode" in your browser settings. This automatically suspends inactive tabs, freeing up RAM for Photoshop. It’s a simple toggle, but it stops that freezing sensation when you have twenty tabs open.

For Photoshop itself, the biggest bottleneck is usually the scratch disk. If your main drive is full, Photoshop slows down drastically. Go to Edit > Preferences > Scratch Disks and make sure you have a secondary drive selected if you have one. If you only have one drive, try to keep at least 20GB of free space on it. Also, check your cache levels. Reducing the number of cache levels from the default (usually 4 or 8) down to 2 or 3 can sometimes speed up rendering on older CPUs.

Another quick win is disabling GPU acceleration if your graphics card is struggling. Go to Edit > Preferences > Performance
